paperTitle: O-Level English — Basic Band Practice 02: The Fan
provenanceNote: NOT STUDENT-FACING. Basic band (2026-08-14). Original narrative written for the morning-quiz bank; NOT from any past exam paper. Spec: ~250-word passage, high-frequency vocabulary, short sentences, 5 questions / 5 marks, 3 of them click-only. Q1-Q2 short answer (1-4 words), Q3 vocabulary in context, Q4 literal, Q5 feeling — all MCQ.

sections.instruction: Read the story below and answer the questions that follow. [2 marks]. Write short answers. One or two words are enough.
sections.passage:
Paragraph 1
Our classroom is on the top floor. In the afternoon the sun sits on the roof and the room turns into an oven.

Paragraph 2
We have four fans. In March, the one above my desk stopped turning. Nobody said anything. We just moved our chairs.

Paragraph 3
By the second week, the back row was empty. Everyone had squeezed to the front, under the three fans that still worked.

Paragraph 4
My friend Hafiz said, 'Somebody should tell the office.' We all agreed. Then we all did nothing.

Paragraph 5
On Friday I stayed back to finish my homework. The room was quiet. I looked up at the dead fan and finally walked downstairs.

Paragraph 6
The lady at the office wrote down my class and the fan number. It took her about thirty seconds. She thanked me.

Paragraph 7
On Monday a man came with a ladder. When he climbed down he saw me and smiled. It was Uncle Raj from my block. He fixes lifts and fans for the town council.

Paragraph 8
'Three weeks,' he said, shaking his head. 'You know how long the repair takes? Twenty minutes.'

Paragraph 9
I think about that a lot now. The hard part was never the fan.

questions.stem: Q1. From Paragraph 2, in which month did the fan stop turning? [1]
Q2. From Paragraph 7, what does Uncle Raj repair for the town council? [1]

questions.stem: Q3. In Paragraph 1, the writer says the room 'turns into an oven'. What does this tell us? [1]

options.text: Food is cooked in the room.

questions.stem: Q4. Why was the back row empty by the second week? [1]

options.text: Those students had left the school.
The teacher moved them to the front.
Everyone moved forward to sit under the working fans.
The back row was being repaired.

questions.stem: Q5. In Paragraph 9, what has the writer learnt? [1]

options.text: Fans break more often than lifts.
Speaking up was easier than waiting.
The office staff work too slowly.
He should sit in the front row.
